title: The lost sheep
summary: The shepherd leaves everything to look for one single sheep. In Zion, a child has left the game, sad and alone: go and find him!

trait.name: Love that seeks
trait.description: Loving like God means leaving no one out: we go and find the one who is alone, lost or forgotten.
trait.jesus: Jesus went to the people everyone avoided, like Zacchaeus, whom nobody liked. He said: "I came to seek and to save the lost."

objectives.intro: Go and see the Keeper, at the foot of the tower.
objectives.missing: Some children are playing by the fountain: go and talk to Lea.
objectives.search: Find Timothy and bring him back to the fountain square.
objectives.party: Go back to Lea and the children.

intro.text: Do you know how many people live in Zion? Lots! And yet God knows each one by name.
Listen to this story Jesus told.

missing.text: Hi! We're playing ring-a-roses, but there are only three of us…
Timothy used to play with us. But we laughed at him because he runs slowly… So he left.
Maybe he's hiding somewhere near the city walls. Nobody went to look for him.

found.text: What are you doing here? Nobody wants me…
That's not true. I came here just for you. Without you, someone is missing!
Really? Well… OK, I'll come with you.

back.text: Timothy is back at the fountain square.

party.text: Timothy! You're back! We're sorry we laughed at you.
Come and join the circle! Let's play a game where everyone can win.
Thank you for looking for me… I feel like I belong again.

debrief.text: There is joy in Zion today, just as there is joy in heaven when someone comes back to God.
The shepherd didn't say: "Never mind, I still have ninety-nine." To him, every sheep mattered.
Jesus is like that shepherd. He never forgets us. And he teaches us to go and find those who are alone.

panels.text: Jesus says: "Imagine a shepherd who has a hundred sheep. He knows them all, and he loves them all."
"One evening, he counts them: ninety-seven, ninety-eight, ninety-nine… One is missing!"
"The shepherd leaves the ninety-nine others safe. He goes off into the hills to look for the lost one, until he finds it."
"When he finds it, he is filled with joy! He puts it on his shoulders and carries it home."
"He calls his friends: Rejoice with me, I have found my lost sheep!"
Jesus explains: "There is great joy in heaven over one single person who comes back to God." To God, everyone is precious.

lea.text: Good luck! Look carefully behind the houses, near the walls.

samy.text: We're waiting for Timothy to start again.

ana.text: Do you think he'll want to come back?

ending.message: To God, nobody is one too many and nobody is forgotten. Like Jesus, we can go and find the one who is alone and tell them: you matter!
ending.reflection: The shepherd could have settled for his ninety-nine sheep. Who around us risks being forgotten or left out, perhaps because of a difference or a disability? What could we do, concretely, to reach out to them?

life.bibleWhere: Luke is in the New Testament, after Matthew and Mark. Find chapter 15. Right after, Jesus also tells of the lost coin and the lost son: three stories of what is found!
life.bibleQuestion: What does the shepherd do when he finds his sheep? And what does he do when he gets home?
life.prayer: Jesus, thank you for coming to look for me and never forgetting me. Show me who is alone around me, and give me the courage to go to them. Amen.
life.challenge: This week, go to someone who is alone (at school, at church, in your neighbourhood) and invite them to play or talk with you.
life.followup: So, did you go to someone who was alone? How did it go?
life.verse: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.
family: For little ones: how many sheep did the shepherd have? How many were missing?
For older ones: why does just one sheep matter so much to the shepherd?
For everyone: how could we welcome someone who feels alone or different?
life.activity: Hide a little sheep (paper or soft toy) in the house. Whoever finds it tells someone why they matter to God.
